title: token-span-heuristic-scrapbook
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick personal scratchpad for token/span-level cleanup heuristics I'm testing. Goal is to capture a few non-obvious rules that keep coming up during small-batch audits and triage sessions. Not a final guide — mostly observations, sample sentences, and open questions to raise with labeling team next week.

High-level principles I'm leaning toward:
- Prefer conservative, model-friendly spans: when in doubt, include minimal contiguous tokens that capture the entity intent.
- Keep label semantics consistent with downstream evaluation: if downstream metric relies on exact string match for normalization, prefer canonical tokenization anchors (see examples).
- Annotate nested or overlapping spans only when they're semantically distinct for the task. Avoid over-labeling.

Common trouble areas and heuristic notes:
1) Email-like / user handles vs. free text
- Raw examples: alice.smith+prod@company.co, user_1234@, @service-bot, service.bot@company (trailing punctuation)
- Heuristic: label full contiguous email-like token excluding trailing punctuation (. , ; : ? ! ) unless punctuation is inside the token (plus sign, underscore, dot).
- Edge: ambiguous trailing parenthesis: (reach out to ops (ops-team@company.com)). Label 'ops-team@company.com' without surrounding parens.

2) IDs and product codes with mixed punctuation
- Examples: PRJ-230_0x1a, case#9923, invoice: INV/2024-0007, 0xdeadbeef
- Heuristic: treat hyphen/underscore/slash as part of code if there's an alpha prefix or consistent pattern. If it's a natural-language phrase with dash (e.g., "user-facing"), do NOT label as code.
- Rationale: many models break tokens at punctuation; keeping code as single span improves normalization.

3) Phone numbers and short numeric tokens in prose
- Examples: +1 (415) 555-0123, 415-555-0123 x22, 5550123 (ambiguous), 412 13 55 (not a phone)
- Heuristic: require at least 7 consecutive digits (ignoring formatting chars) plus an explicit country/code or context hint ("call", "tel"). Otherwise mark as NUMBER only if task supports it.

4) Hyphenation and compound nouns
- Examples: high-level, out-of-the-box, A/B-test, COVID-19, pre-existing
- Heuristic: if hyphen joins two lexical units that together form a semantic unit ("high-level"), annotate whole hyphenated span. Exceptions: adjectival constructions where first is a modifier that is not an entity itself — still annotate entire token if it's labeled in task.

5) Bracketed metadata and inline citations
- Examples: "(see section 2.1)", "[note: internal]", "file (v2)"
- Heuristic: do NOT include surrounding brackets in the span unless the bracket content is the thing to be labeled (e.g., code inside brackets). Trim surrounding punctuation.

6) Overlapping spans: person names inside organization names
- Example: "OpenAI Research — John Doe lab"
- Heuristic: annotate organization span "OpenAI Research" and person "John Doe" separately. Avoid creating a single overlapping span that merges both. If labeling schema forbids overlaps, prefer separate non-overlapping choices with priority: PERSON < ORG (priority means we annotate both but convert to non-overlapping by splitting or excluding the smaller one depending on downstream need).

7) Time ranges and ambiguous connectors
- Examples: "10-12pm", "10 - 12 pm", "10 to 12"
- Heuristic: label the entire contiguous time expression as TIME. Normalize later during preprocessing.

8) URLs with query strings and fragments
- Examples: https://app.redwood.ai/run?job=123&env=prod#metrics, http://example.com/, example.com/path
- Heuristic: label the full URL token including query and fragment. If URL appears inline followed by punctuation, drop trailing punctuation.

Representative annotated samples (toy format: sentence -> [span:LABEL notes])
1) "Spoke with john.doe@example.com about the PRJ-230_0x1a ticket." -> [john.doe@example.com:EMAIL full email, trim trailing punctuation] [PRJ-230_0x1a:CODE include underscore]
2) "Deployed v2.3-beta to staging (rollback tested)." -> [v2.3-beta:VERSION include hyphen and beta]
3) "Contact +1 (415) 555-0123 x22 for Ops." -> [+1 (415) 555-0123 x22:PHONE include extension if present] [Ops:ORG ambiguous, label only if task expects orgs]
4) "See file README.md (v1)." -> [README.md:FILENAME include .md] [v1:VERSION inside parens decide if needed]
5) "Customer: Acme Corp — point of contact: Jane A. Doe, jr." -> [Acme Corp:ORG] [Jane A. Doe:PERSON note suffix 'jr' consider attach if contiguous]

Tokenization mismatch notes (things to watch in audits)
- Subword breaks: contracted forms (don't -> do n't) can make span boundaries weird for exact-match evaluation. When downstream uses detokenized strings, prefer annotating based on surface (white-space and punctuation) rather than subword tokens.
- Unicode variants: nonbreaking spaces or zero-width joiners in paste'd samples cause span misses. Quick audit check: normalize whitespace in raw text before evaluating.

Open questions / stuff to bring up:
- Overlaps policy: do we allow overlapping spans in dataset format? If not, what's canonical priority ordering? Current options: ORG > PERSON > CODE > EMAIL. Need sign-off from product on evaluation mapping.
- Should we split hyphenated versions as separate labels for normalization ("v2.3-beta" -> VERSION with normalized form "2.3 beta")? Evals look at normalized value more than raw span.
- Ambiguity in short numeric tokens: are invoice numbers (4-digit) considered CODE even if short? Propose threshold + context rules.

Quick checklist for triage sessions:
- Paste raw example into "sanity strip" tool: normalize whitespace, collapse zero-width chars.
- Run tokenizer preview and inspect subword splits for candidate spans.
- If subword split breaks label awkwardly, adjust span to include full orthographic token.
- Log examples into JIRA with prefix LABELER-EXAMPLE and attach tokenization screenshot.

Notes to self: keep this light and iterative. Collect 50 'weird' examples from audits and make a short one-pager with priority decisions. Plan: bring top 10 to labeling sync on 2025-01-12.

Random scratch examples to copy into audit queue:
- "Reached out to ops@vendor.inc; they replied 03/11/24."
- "ref: INV/2024-0007 — see attachment."
- "user: @jlee-dev, alias: jlee.dev"
- "Open-source pre-release v0.9.0-alpha"
- "matrix id 0x4f3a2b - suspected leak"

End of scratchpad.
(If this turns into a formal doc, split into concise rules + examples + automation tests.)
